narrative.origin_story: Hannah Sørensen runs treasury for a forty-person renewable-energy fintech in Copenhagen.
narrative.manifesto:
Work crossed borders. Finance didn't.

A company in Berlin can find a specialist in São Paulo, a designer in Lagos, an engineer in Bangalore, and a partner in Singapore in a morning. By afternoon, the legal entity, the contract template, the compliance check, the currency conversion, and the payroll cycle are still operating on the calendar of 1985.

We built Bastion to close that gap with the only thing that has ever closed gaps in finance: a serious institutional posture about identity, custody, and settlement.

Identity is the foundation. A Looper earns a Bastion identity once and uses it for life. KYC and KYB completed and refreshed automatically. Reputation accumulated. Audit trail permanent.

Contracts are promises with proof. Digital, versioned, machine-readable, executable. Compliance is automatic.

Treasury is consolidated. Multi-currency accounts, real-time visibility, automatic reconciliation, programmable flows.

Settlement happens at the speed of work. Stablecoin reserves backed 1:1, audited quarterly, insured by Lloyd's of London. Cross-border payment in minutes, not weeks. Local-currency payout in the contractor's preferred channel.

Everything is published. Reserves are audited and visible. The Trust Center is the front door, not the footer.

This is what serious financial infrastructure has always done. We did it again, this time for work that no longer fits inside one country.
